description: 12V to 5V switching regulator module
notes: 3-pin SIP on a 7805 footprint - no inductor, no feedback network, no layout risk. ONE: the one dev board, the 8x8 matrix and the level shifter (ADR 0015 - there is no display board). Its share of the clamp-legal worst case is 68-78% of 1A (power-entry-instrument.md). IT IS 10.4mm TALL UPRIGHT, which fits anywhere on the main board, under the key boards included (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board parts room under the key boards' and 'regulator block fits where it stands') - no need to lay it flat. *** MINIMUM INPUT IS 8V FOR THE 5.0V PART, NOT THE 7V ON THE FEATURES LINE - THAT 7V IS THE 3.3V PART'S. *** The front page says 'Wide input range (7V - 28V)' and the selection table says R-78E3.3-1.0 = 7-28, R-78E5.0-1.0 = 8-28. Not binding here - worst case at the buck input is ~10.96V (rack at 11.4V, less ~0.28V of Schottky, ~36mV of R-ILIM and FET, ~121mV in 4m of Cat5 at 360mA), so ~3V of margin and even a 20% rack sag clears it - but anyone sizing the umbilical against '7V' is working to the wrong part. DERATING: 100% of rated load from -40C to +60C ambient, then linear to 60% at +85C with a hard cutoff, natural convection. At 65C ambient that permits 92% against the 69-78% actually drawn, ~14 points of margin, and 78% stays legal to ~73.8C. SWITCHING FREQUENCY 330kHz for the 3.3V and 5V outputs (570kHz for 12V) - the figure C-AA-ADC is sized against. Max capacitive load 220uF. No minimum load on the 5V part. Short-circuit protection is CONTINUOUS WITH AUTOMATIC RECOVERY, not latching. BUY RECOM'S OWN (LCSC C3033024, or a distributor): the in-stock parts LCSC lists under the same number from other makers switch at 520-850 kHz, not 330 kHz [web LCSC listings, 2026-09-29], and C-AA-ADC is sized against 330 kHz. Hand-soldered (THT)

notes: Bulk belongs at the load. A ferrite is a wire at the WS2815's ~2kHz PWM rate. ONE: one strip, fed on the main board beside J-LED (ADR 0016). UCW1E471MNL1GS (LCSC C340751): 25 V on the 12 V strip feed

description: LC between the umbilical node and the buck input
notes: A real inductor, not a bead. SWPA6028S220MT (LCSC C51349), 22 uH: the value the input LC's derivation uses (power-entry-instrument.md)

description: ORs USB VBUS with the umbilical-derived 5V rail for bench use
notes: One diode from the buck into the dev board's 5V node, which USB VBUS also feeds. Bench affordance for E5, explicitly not a standalone mode. SS14-E3/61T (LCSC C47460): SMA like D-REVSHUNT's SMC, so machine-placed with no hand step, and 2.29 max high [ds SS14.pdf p.3], inside the main board's SMD height. VF 0.50 V max at 1 A [ds p.2]; at 0.7-0.8 A it drops about 0.45 V, leaving about 4.55 V at the dev board's 5V pin - fine for its 3V3 LDO [calc]. Dissipation 0.78 A x 0.45 V = 0.35 W, +31 C at RthJA 88 C/W [calc, ds p.2]. The breath sensor is not on this rail

description: Bulk cap at the umbilical entry / buck input - the C of L-BUCK-IN's LC
notes: Completes the LC: L-BUCK-IN had an L and no C. One buck and one capacitor. Also the capacitance the module load switch's inrush ramp is sized against (ADR 0005). 25V part on a 12V rail for derating. UCM1E101MCL1GS (LCSC C729678): AN ELECTROLYTIC, NEVER A CERAMIC - its ESR is the LC's damping (power-entry-instrument.md, the input LC)

description: TVS across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: 15V standoff on a 12V rail. The power pair is the one the old 6-channel array could never have covered - six channels against eight conductors, and the six non-power ones are the natural fit

description: Shunt diode across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: UNRETROFITTABLE. A rollover/console RJ45 lead swaps 3 and 6, which on the T568B map are +12V and PWR_GND - reverse polarity into the instrument, from a consumable patch lead that looks identical to a good one. Cathode to the +12V pin: reversed, it conducts hard, the module's LT1641-1 sees a short and LATCHES OFF, and the panel LED says so - the load switch becomes the fuse. *** PACKAGE IS DO-214AB (SMC), NOT DO-214AC *** [SS34.pdf p.1, 'MECHANICAL DATA / Case: SMC (DO-214AB)']. DO-214AC is the SS14's package, and the two are a footprint apart on unretrofittable reverse-polarity protection sitting on the +12V pin - check it against the drawing before the board goes out

description: The analog star's single tie: AGND_INST to PWR_GND at one point
notes: COPPER, NOT A PART: nothing is bought or placed. The layout puts it at the analog star point, the one place AGND_INST meets PWR_GND (carrier.md section 2; dig-gnd-topology), and the net tie lets KiCad's DRC allow that join there and nowhere else. Assembly: none

description: 5.000V precision series reference for the breath sensor supply
notes: The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric, so ITS SUPPLY IS ITS SCALE FACTOR - that is the whole reason for a separate reference here. Buffered by half of U-BUF, and see R-ISO-REF for the network that makes that buffer stable. *** THE GRADE IS A LIVE, TRACKED DISPUTE: see ref5050-grade, and do not restate its numbers here. *** The short of it is that the A suffix is the WORSE grade [Table 4-2 p.3: REF50xxI = 'High', REF50xxAI = 'Standard'], which is the opposite of what a reader expects from a letter suffix, and the fix is one letter in the order code for the same package and pinout. FETCH NOTE for whoever needs the document again: ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ref5050.pdf is a REAL 404 - TI renamed the folder REF50XX -> REF50/REF50E at rev O and broke the symlink - and the working URL is ti.com/lit/ds/sbos410/sbos410.pdf

description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8, and it RUNS ON +12V, NOT 5V: a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is then at the rail, so there is no clamp current and the >=3.3k protection-resistor requirement goes away. Same part as the module op-amps - DEVICE FACTS ARE ON U-OPA-PITCH and are not repeated here. STABILITY IS THE WHOLE OF THIS ROW. The reference half drives the sensor's 100nF decoupler ALONE - C-REF-OUT is on the REF5050, not on this output (see figures.yaml cref-out-node). Against the specified 375 ohm open-loop Zo that is 1.5 degrees of phase margin as a bare follower, so IT MUST BE COMPENSATED, with TI's own dual-feedback network [SBOS737C Figure 56]: R-ISO-REF 37.4R, R-FB-REF 10k taken at VS, R-FBX-REF 100R + C-FB-REF 1nF at this pin. That gives 85.9 degrees AND exactly zero DC error across R-ISO-REF, so the 2% ratiometric objection to an out-of-loop resistor never has to be paid - see figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: Output and input capacitors on the REF5050
notes: REF5050 VIN bypass and REF5050 VOUT load capacitor - one each, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside each. *** NEITHER IS ON THE BUFFER'S OUTPUT *** (see figures.yaml cref-out-node); this is the rail that IS the breath scale factor. The VOUT one is not a choice - the part cannot be built without it [SBOS410O 8.4.1 p.26: 'Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the ESR value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm', with Figure 8-6 giving CL = 1uF to 50uF] - and the other is the 8.4.1 supply bypass (1-10uF). That accounts for both and leaves nothing for the buffer output, which is just as well: 10uF there would be 10000x the OPA2197's 1 nF capacitive-load limit. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: the REF5050 now drives only the OPA2197's input bias current (+/-20 pA max at 25C), so its load regulation (20 ppm/mA typ, 30 max, 50 over temperature) contributes ZERO to the breath scale factor, where the other topology would have cost 300 ppm = 1.0 LSB. THE SERIES 1-1.5 OHM RESISTOR IS OPTIONAL, NOT REQUIRED - 8.4.1's 'ESR <= 1.5 ohm' is a stability CEILING an X7R satisfies trivially, and 9.4.1.1 p.29 says plainly 'A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional.' FIT A 0R/1R0 FOOTPRINT and decide it at E13 with a scope; it is electrically free either way, being in series with a capacitor to ground rather than in the signal path. The TRIM/NR 1uF is DECLINED: 8.3.6 p.26 halves 4.5 uVrms to 2.25 uVrms and lengthens start-up, on a term already 325x below an ADC LSB (4.5 uVrms against 1.46 mV)

description: Isolation resistor, reference buffer dual-feedback network (SBOS737C Fig. 56)
notes: OPA2197 output to U-BREATH VS (pin 2). One of four parts in TI's dual-feedback reference-buffer network [SBOS737C 8.2.3 p.30, Figure 56 'Precision Reference Buffer']; the other three are R-FB-REF, R-FBX-REF and C-FB-REF. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE. *** TI'S FIGURE TRANSFERS TO OUR 100 nF DESPITE ITS 10uF BECAUSE R_ISO IS SET BY Zo, NOT BY C_L *** - the attenuation R_ISO/(Zo+R_ISO) and the pole-zero ratio both depend only on R_ISO/Zo, and C_L moves both corners together and cancels. 37.4R is Zo/10 against the specified 375 ohm (see U-OPA-PITCH). Simulated 85.9 degrees at 896 kHz; the same model run on Figure 56 as printed returns 87.4 against TI's published 89. *** DC ERROR ACROSS THIS RESISTOR IS EXACTLY ZERO BY TOPOLOGY *** - C-FB-REF blocks at DC so no current flows in R-FBX-REF, input current is pA so none flows in R-FB-REF, and the amplifier therefore forces V(VS) = 5.000 V. Its value and tolerance stop mattering; the 1% is bought for stock reasons. Power is (10mA)^2 x 37.4 = 3.74 mW in an 0805. DO NOT PUT R_ISO INSIDE THE LOOP: it buys nothing at ANY value - 1.5 degrees at 10R and 1.5 degrees at 37.4R, the same as fitting nothing. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: DC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the sensor's VS pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 10k AND NOT TI'S 1M, deliberately. Two reasons TI's circuit does not have. (1) The guaranteed-over-temperature I_B of 5 nA through 1M is 5 mV = 1000 ppm = 3.4 LSB on a rail that IS the ratiometric scale factor; through 10k it is 50 uV = 0.034 LSB. (2) R_F x C_F sets the HANDOVER frequency above which the loop closes on the amplifier's own output instead of on VS. TI's load is a pure capacitor; ours draws 10 mA, so above the handover any load-current change appears at VS across R-ISO-REF. TI's 1M x 39nF puts it at 4.08 Hz, inside the breath channel. 10k x 1nF puts it at 15.9 kHz, well above the 500 Hz channel, and |Z_out| at VS is then 1.20 ohm at 500 Hz. The R-FB-REF:R-FBX-REF RATIO OF 100:1 IS WHAT MUST BE PRESERVED from TI, not the absolute values

description: AC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the OPA2197 output pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | Scales with R-FB-REF to hold TI's 100:1 ratio, so that above the handover the loop closes on the amplifier output with only 1% of VS leaking in. R_Fx x C_F is 100 ns here against the 3.74 us TI's own rule (R_Fx C_F = R_ISO C_L) would give, and the simulation says it costs nothing - the binding condition is |R_Fx + 1/(2.pi.f C_F)| much less than R_F AT CROSSOVER, which at 896 kHz is 100 + 178 = 205 ohm against 10k, a 49x margin

description: AC feedback capacitor, reference buffer
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | C0G, because this capacitor sets the handover frequency and an X7R's DC-bias and temperature derating would move it. 1nF at R-FB-REF's 10k gives a 15.9 kHz handover. IT IS ALSO WHY THE DC ERROR IS ZERO: blocking at DC is what leaves R-FB-REF as the only feedback path, so the amplifier servos the SENSOR pin rather than its own output. NOTE FOR THE SPICE DECK: this network leaves the summing node with no DC path except through R-FB-REF, so a simulator needs a leak resistor there for convergence and a real board does not - the amplifier's input leakage provides it

description: Series resistor ahead of the REF5050 input, into the zener clamp
notes: +12V to REF_VIN. THE RAIL'S TVS DOES NOT PROTECT THE REFERENCE: D-TVS-PWR clamps at up to 24.4 V [ds LITTELFUSE-SMAJ-SERIES-SMAJ15A.pdf p.2] and the REF5050's VIN abs max is 18 V [ds REF5050.pdf p.5]. This resistor limits the zener's current to (24.4 - 15.75)/330 = 26 mA [calc]. DC drop at the reference's 1.2 mA max [ds REF5050.pdf p.8] is 0.40 V, leaving >= 11.6 V against 5.2 V needed [ds p.7]. The REF5050's VIN capacitors sit on REF_VIN, after this resistor, so R and C filter ahead of the clamp. Same part as R-LED-SER (UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F3300T5E).

description: 15 V zener clamp on the REF5050 input (MMSZ5245BT1G)
notes: Cathode to REF_VIN, anode to AGND_INST. Vz 14.25-15.75 V at 8.5 mA, Zzt 16 ohm max [ds ONSEMI-MMSZ5221BT1-SERIES-MMSZ5245BT1G.pdf p.3]: at 26 mA it holds <= 16.1 V, under the REF5050's 18 V [calc]. Leakage is specified only at 11 V (0.1 uA); 1 uA through R-REF-IN would be 0.33 mV, so it cannot move the reference [calc].

description: Anti-alias cap at the MCP3202 input pin
notes: 564Hz with the divider's 6k Thevenin (10k||15k) - matches the 500Hz channel everywhere else. WAS 220nF, which is 121Hz and smears the breath band; the '~600Hz, 58dB at 496kHz' note was wrong twice over - wrong corner, and the R-78E5.0 switches at 330kHz not 496kHz. 55dB at 330kHz. C0G not X7R in a DC-accurate path

description: Bulk at MCP3202 VDD/VREF
notes: DRAWN ON THE PAGE AND MISSING FROM THIS BOM UNTIL 2026-09-22. *** PROPOSED, NOT DECIDED *** - the page says so and this row says so. The MCP3202 has no VREF anti-alias and the WS2815 PWM is ~2 kHz against a 4 kHz sample rate, so reference ripple aliases straight into the breath reading. DECIDED AT E9, on the bench, by scoping VREF with the LEDs sweeping - that is the only measurement that settles whether this part is needed at all and whether 10uF is enough. IF FITTED, 1206: Samsung CL31B106KBHNNNE (LCSC C89632), 10 uF X7R 50 V - the same part as C-REF-OUT, so no new line

description: Lower leg of the 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: LOWER LEG, to the instrument analog star. 15k against the 10k upper leg is the 0.6x that lands sensor-full-scale inside a 3V3 ADC's range. The RATIO is what matters, so buy both legs from one reel

description: Upper leg of the 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: UPPER LEG, AND >=10k IS THE SPEC, NOT THE VALUE: below that, 5V-before-3V3 sequencing pushes about 2.5 mA into the ADC's ESD clamp on every power-up. It also has to leave C-AA-ADC time to settle, which is what stops the leg going higher still. Divide AFTER the buffer, never before

description: 12-bit 2-ch SAR ADC SPI
notes: SOIC-8. VDD-referenced so no separate ref chip. 50ksps at 3V3 vs 4-8kHz needed. One spare channel | 2026-09-21, from Microchip DS21034F now at datasheets/analog/MCP3202-CI-SN.pdf: fCLK max is 1.8MHz at VDD=5V and 0.9MHz at VDD=2.7V, WITH NO 3.3V ROW. The 0.9MHz the design uses is therefore the GUARANTEED 2.7V MAXIMUM, not an interpolation - two documents called it an interpolation and it is strictly conservative at 3.3V, with ~25% of unclaimed headroom (straight-line to 3.3V gives ~1.14MHz). Both rows are characterised, not 100% tested. ALSO A MINIMUM NOBODY HAD: the sample cap holds charge for at least 1.2ms at 85C, so effective fCLK >= ~10kHz - which forecloses 'slow the ADC down' as a way to buy loop time. Sample cap 20pF with 1k switch resistance; tSAMPLE is 1.5 clock cycles and source impedance adds directly to it, so the buffer ahead of it is load-bearing

description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3.3V reads high. ONE GATE USED, THREE SPARE (ADR 0016 - one strip); tie every spare input. The WS2815 datasheet's own recommended application circuit GROUNDS the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5), so only DI is driven. WS2815 THRESHOLD VERIFIED: V_IH = 0.7 x VDD in a table whose header declares VDD = 4.5-5.5V, so 3.15-3.85V, which this part clears at 5V. Do not read that VDD as the +12V LED rail

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 IN AND OUT, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there | 2026-09-21: QTY 7 -> 8. The old enumeration gave the REF5050 one 100nF while carrier.md drew one at its OUTPUT and the prose claimed one at the sensor's VS pin - the same part spent twice across three files, and none drawn at VS at all. SBOS410O section 9.4.1.1 pp.29-30 wants both: a VIN bypass AND 'a high-frequency, 1uF capacitor in parallel between the output and ground'. Settled allocation is REF5050 VIN, REF5050 VOUT, and U-BREATH VS (pin 2) - and the VS one is the 100 nF the reference buffer's compensation is designed against. See figures.yaml cref-out-node

description: Series resistor on the WS2815 data line at the driver
notes: Damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. ONE: one strip (ADR 0016). BI is NOT driven - the datasheet (datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf) grounds the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5), so it needs no gate and no resistor. The figure is a raster with no text layer and was read by rendering at 700dpi - confirm visually before wiring

description: Pull-down on the LED data line at the MCU pin
notes: IO1 is high-impedance through the bootloader window, and a floating WS2815 data line is the classic source of intermittent LED behaviour. WHAT DECIDES IT: E1, where the strip first runs - if the boot window shows no spurious pixels without it, it is not needed. One part, one strip (ADR 0016)

description: WS2815 strip: DI, BI, +12V, GND
package: 4 plated holes, drill 1.0 (THT pads, no part)
notes: Four conductors: DI through R-LED-SER, BI, and strip power. *** BI IS A GROUND CONNECTION, NOT A DRIVEN ONE *** - see the page; wiring it as a second data line is the mistake these pads invite. The +12V and GND pads carry strip power but that net belongs to carrier/power-entry-instrument, not to this circuit. PADS, NOT A CONNECTOR: the strip lies on the same board (ADR 0016), so its leads solder straight in. A plug would add 7-10 mm of height and a pigtail loop [ds JST-XH-SERIES.pdf p.1] to guard against a reversal that, with pads, can only happen once - at the build. SILKSCREEN EACH PAD 12V / DI / BI / GND, SQUARE PAD ON GND, AND CHECK 12V-TO-GND WITH A METER BEFORE FIRST POWER: reversed, 12V goes into the gate driver's output. Replacing the strip means desoldering four leads

description: Service header: the real-time board's U0TXD, U0RXD, GND, EN and IO0
notes: FIVE PINS (ADR 0018): 1 TXD (IO43, out), 2 RXD (IO44, in), 3 GND, 4 EN, 5 IO0 - the ground between the UART pair and the control pair. EN and IO0 reach it on two conductors of CBL-MCU-RIBBON, soldered on the Matrix to its Key1 (RESET/EN) and Key2 (BOOT/IO0) terminals. NOTHING IN SERIES: the Matrix pulls both up with 10k to its 3V3 (R8, R10) and its buttons pull them to GND [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf]. DRIVE THEM TO GROUND ONLY - a button, a jumper, or an adapter's open-collector reset circuit; never drive them high, least of all from a 5V adapter. Recovery order: USB-Serial-JTAG through the tail USB-C first, a reflash over the same port second, this header third - and with EN and IO0 here, download mode can be forced in place (firmware/README.md)

description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
package: dev board, on the lid; CBL-MCU-RIBBON soldered to its pad rows
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 17 GPIO on its two pad rows (1-7, 33-40, 43, 44) and 12 used; CBL-MCU-RIBBON takes them to J-MCU. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM, both on-package: the vendor schematic marks U66 = ESP32-S3FH4R2 [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; F=in-package flash, H4=4MB, R2=2MB quad PSRAM from Espressif's ordering code, from memory], so GPIO33-37 are free - octal PSRAM would have taken them. The 8x8 matrix is the instrument's only display, under a window in the top face (ADR 0015) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003). THE SENSOR IS SOLDERED TO THE BOARD AND COATED WITH IT: a sensor swap breaks the coating at its eight joints - re-mask both ports before touching it up

part: 2-layer PCB - the main board: thumb switches, both thumb registers and the carrier circuits
description: Thumb switches and their registers, breath sensor, reference, ADC, umbilical, SPI egress, LED-strip drive and strip, the regulator, service header
package: long and narrow, sized in mechanical/drc.echo (main board), 1.6mm (config/body.yaml switch.pcb_t)
notes: ONE board at the thumb level, mouth cap to the end of the right hand (ADR 0017). A TONGUE runs on from its tail end to the etherCON's adapter and carries J-UMB, soldered into both (ADR 0021). The thumb switches solder into it; the key boards connect to it by 12-conductor IDC ribbons (CBL-CHAIN), a through-hole right-angle J-CHAIN header for each in its far band beside the LED strip. Parts face up - mechanical/drc.echo gives the room under the key boards and elsewhere. Holes over the U-bolt nuts, notches at the screws, and a hole at each mount - on a thumb plate the key boards' stud, spacer and nut, on the oak an insert, a spacer and a screw (ADR 0022). 1.6mm, as the key boards, its top pressed against the thumb switches' housing bottom (ADR 0020 Amendment 6). Long: check the board house's panel and price before M4. Nothing on it is fast or RF - 2 layers, hand-assembled

description: The Matrix's connector on the main board: CBL-MCU-RIBBON plugs in here and unplugs when the lid comes off
notes: WHERE: the main board's tail end beside the regulator block, side entry, the ribbon arriving level from the mouth side; the LED strip stops short of it (mechanical/DESIGN.md). PINOUT (ADR 0018), ribbon conductor n = pin n [IDC numbering, from memory - confirm on the socket's drawing]: 1 5V, 2 GND, 3 5V, 4 IO1, 5 IO2 (spare), 6 IO7, 7 IO3 (spare), 8 IO38, 9 GND, 10 IO35, 11 GND, 12 IO36, 13 3V3, 14 IO34, 15 GND, 16 IO39, 17 5V, 18 IO37, 19 IO33, 20 IO40, 21 IO44 (RX), 22 IO43 (TX), 23 IO0, 24 EN. hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative. Every fast line - IO35 SCLK, IO36 MOSI, IO34 CS_MOD, IO38 chain SCK, IO7 SH/LD - has a ground, a supply or a static line on both sides; pin 9 is the ground between SCLK (IO35) and the chain clock (IO38). EN is on the edge with only IO0 beside it: the Matrix has no capacitor on EN (R8 10k to 3V3 and Key1 to GND, nothing else - datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf). IO2 and IO3 are spare and reach no other part on the main board; bring them to two test pads beside J-MCU. KEYED AND SHROUDED: a reversed plug puts 5V on a GPIO. RATING: the 5V and GND contacts carry the whole Matrix draw, and fed from the 5V pad nothing on the Matrix limits it (its USB diode is bypassed - matrix-led-current, power_path), so rate them against U-BUCK's 1A (R-78E5.0-1.0), not against matrix-led-current: three 5V contacts at ~0.33A and four GND at ~0.25A each [calc, equal sharing], against ~1A per 1.27mm contact [from memory]. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: 1.27mm dual-row box headers with a 0.635mm-ribbon IDC mate are a stock family; the envelope is from memory too]. Decided at M4 with the part in hand: the envelope, the latch and the mating IDC socket

part: 24-way flat ribbon, 0.635mm pitch, with a 2x12 1.27mm IDC socket at one end
description: The Matrix's wiring: soldered to its two pad rows, two test pads and its two button pads on the lid, plugged into J-MCU on the main board
notes: CONDUCTORS: 24, conductor n = J-MCU pin n (J-MCU row; hardware/carrier/netlist.yaml is authoritative). AT THE MATRIX END [datasheets/mechanical/WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-SCHEMATIC.pdf; pad rows per WAVESHARE-ESP32-S3-MATRIX-pinout.png]: the 12 used GPIO and the spare IO2 and IO3 to their pads; 3V3 (13) to the 3V3 pad; 5V x3 - conductors 1 and 3 both on the 5V pad, 17 on TP2 (net VCC_5V); GND x4 - conductor 2 on the GND pad, 9, 11 and 15 on TP3 (net GND). IF TP3 WILL NOT TAKE THREE JOINTS, twist 9, 11 and 15 together and tin them as one joint - each is still its own path to J-MCU. EN (24) to Key1 and IO0 (23) to Key2, each on the terminal that goes to its 10k pull-up (R8 for RESET/EN, R10 for IO0), NOT the one on GND: with a meter, the right terminal reads ~10k to the 3V3 pad and the wrong one 0 ohm to the GND pad. A hop is NOT a lumped load (output transition is published as a maximum only, p.8, and a hop is longer than key-chain-loom.md's length rule allows even at that maximum); it does not need to be: QH to the next SER is data sampled a whole clock period later, into a Schmitt input (setup and hold, p.7), and the edge-sensitive SCK and SH/LD are the MCU's, behind R-CHAIN-SER (E14). A board house substitute must have Schmitt-trigger inputs with no transition-rate limit: a 74HC165 or a 74LV165A (whose Schmitt action still carries a rate limit, datasheets/logic/74LV165A-nexperia.pdf p.5) is not one. The thresholds are those figures' threshold_note, not restated here. *** DO NOT JUSTIFY THIS PART BY THE COUPLING ARGUMENT: IT IS WRONG (see ADR 0001). *** A capacitive divider cannot exceed the aggressor's swing, and on the real 5V data line an unfiltered wire sees 1.36V of swing, landing the idle node at 1.94V - above the register's VT- even at its maximum, which is at most 0.5 x VCC in every row TI publishes, 1.65V at 3.3V [calc; datasheets/logic/SN74HCS165-ti-scls828a.pdf p.6]: about 0.3V clear, so an unfiltered wire would not read as a press, but not by much. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec. 1206, 1/4 W: a sustained output fault puts 33 mA through it, 109 mW, which is 87 % of an 0805's 1/8 W and 44 % of this [calc; ds UNIROYAL-THICK-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-0805W8F.pdf, 1206 = 1/4 W, 200 V]. What it does specify is a steady-state ceiling - package dissipation 0.225 W [Abs Max p.2, corroborated 'PD@70degC .225W' p.7]. SO A SUSTAINED FAULT IS NOT SURVIVED BY A BIGGER ARRAY; the fix is a series resistor or a resettable element. ALL FOUR CHANNELS SHARE ONE COMMON PIN (pin 2), to PWR_GND at J-UMB. U-TVS-CHAIN is a second package because it clamps at the J-CHAIN, elsewhere on the main board. THE ARRAY IS EFFECTIVELY UNI-DIRECTIONAL: the -0.8V negative clamp is a forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee. Fine for 0-3.3V SPI; MUST NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node. 30 pF per channel is high for a modern array - against 2 m of Cat5 and R-SPI-SER that is ~29 ns of edge on a 250 ns half-period at 2 MHz, acceptable, and it is the only TVS term in the umbilical edge budget. DO NOT RE-PROPOSE onsemi ESD7104: it is a clean 4-channel 5V array on paper and ships only in UDFN10 and WDFNW10, leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy - as was SP3012-06UTG before it. ORDER -RN2 - NOTCH REVERSED ON THE 2ND (KEY-BOARD) CONNECTOR ONLY (print sheet 2 fig 3). The first socket's cable leaves on the side of its key and the second's on the side away from it; -RN2 reverses the second's notch, so BOTH sockets' cables leave on their key's side (sheet 1 fig 1, sheet 2 fig 3). The main board's header has its key slot facing up, so the MAIN-BOARD SOCKET'S CABLE LEAVES UPWARD; the key board's header is the same part upside down, so the KEY-BOARD SOCKET'S CABLE LEAVES DOWNWARD. The two face each other, the ribbon runs flat with no twist, either end may go on either board, and conductor n meets key-board J-CHAIN pin 13-n. A STANDARD CABLE (no -RN2) FITS AND LOOKS RIGHT: both its ends leave downward, with a half-twist, and conductor 10's 3V3 lands on key-board pin 10, a ground. A cable whose ends both leave downward is wrong. Conductor n is main-board J-CHAIN pin n. Both sockets plug in from the same side, because both headers' mouths face the same way. LENGTH: ORDER FFSD-06-D-<code>-01-N-RN2 where <code> is mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain cable to order (FFSD length code)' - INCHES, overall, over both sockets, with the print's -0.125 in tolerance covered (print sheet 1, note 11). The free length it gives is drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon length (derived)', in mm: never type that into the part number. It lets the lid lie face down beside the body off its far edge, the body standing on its U-bolt, with both sockets plugged in (config/body.yaml routing.chain_service). CLOSED: a flat hairpin along the body, both legs between the two plugs' heights, running the same way to the fold, so it never stands across the LED strip's light (drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon closed: hairpin leg and fold radius', 'key-chain ribbon fold no tighter than its bend radius', 'key-chain ribbon hairpin clear of the lid screws'); which way each folds is routing.chain_fold. Width and thickness: routing.chain_ribbon_w and routing.chain_ribbon_t. TO TAKE THE LID OFF: lift it, lay it beside the body, unplug both sockets. METER EVERY CABLE BEFORE IT IS FIRST POWERED, spares and replacements included: conductor 10 reaches the far socket's position 3 and conductor 2 its position 11 (hardware/boards/key-board-lh/README.md, Bring-up). OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: the part number (with -RN2); boards.chain_plug_proud, measured on the first mated pair, decides whether the cable clears the shroud's mouth

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER
notes: On the main board where the MCU's pins arrive, before anything else on the net. SCK and SH/LD each reach four registers (U-KEYS): right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, and one at the far end of each key board's ribbon, over up to the main board's length (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board (derived)'). At that length an MCU edge sees a line rather than a lump [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. Edge-rate damping at the source - NOT series termination, which ADR 0001 rejected (as R-TERM-CHAIN) for a line that drops on four registers. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER. FIT IT. SIMULATED (hardware/interfaces/key-chain-loom/sim): with it, SCK reaches the left-hand key board's register with no swing back through the register's hysteresis and no overshoot past its clamp at every corner of drive strength, edge rate and load ('sck-to-key-board'); without it, at the strong-drive, fast-edge, light-load corner, SCK swings back through the hysteresis (a double clock) and past the clamp both ways ('sck-without-series-resistor'). The GPIO's output impedance and edge are estimates (Espressif publishes neither, nor IBIS), so E14 still scopes SCK at that register. 1206, 1/4 W: a sustained output fault puts 33 mA through it, 109 mW, which is 87 % of an 0805's 1/8 W and 44 % of this [calc; ds UNIROYAL-THICK-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-0805W8F.pdf, 1206 = 1/4 W, 200 V]. description: Series isolation on the 3V3 conductor of each key board's ribbon, on the main board
notes: ONE PER RIBBON, in series between the main board's 3V3 (DEV_3V3 - the Matrix's ME6217C33M5G LDO, reaching the main board on CBL-MCU-RIBBON) and that ribbon's conductor 10 (main-board J-CHAIN pin 10). right_thumb, left_thumb and R-SER-TERM stay on DEV_3V3 directly. SHORT-CIRCUIT PROTECTION IS THE LDO'S OWN (ADR 0018): datasheets/discrete-and-power/ME6217C33M5G.pdf p.1 'a built-in overcurrent protector' and thermal shutdown at 160C; p.4 Ishort 350mA TYPICAL at VOUT = 0V, with no min or max. PROPOSED: ST LM317LZ, LCSC C5267874. MAP ITS PINS BY NAME: ST numbers the TO-92 1 = ADJ, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT and draws them in the physical order 1-3-2 [ds ST-LM317L-DS2168-REV7.pdf p.4]

description: Series bead per supply branch
notes: One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Chosen on ONE criterion - it is the only >=1A 600R 1206 part found whose datasheet publishes an IMPEDANCE-UNDER-DC-BIAS curve (traces at 0 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 1500 mA). Off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** A BEAD'S CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it says nothing about saturation *** - read the bias curve instead. At 100 MHz this part gives ~614 ohm at 0 A, ~431 at 250 mA, ~157 at 500 mA, ~72 at 1000 mA and ~51 at its RATED 1500 mA. Doubling the rating does not help: a 3000 mA twin in the same package reads ~145 ohm at 500 mA, slightly WORSE, for 0.02 ohm more DCR. PER BRANCH: FB4 (+5V, mA), FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. *** FB2 CARRIES THE UMBILICAL AT figures.yaml umbilical-current AND GETS ROUGHLY HALF THAT *** - ~280-310 ohm, falling to ~245-275 ohm at the module total. No 1206 600R bead of any rating fixes it; bias shifts the impedance peak UP IN FREQUENCY, so the bead does not die, its useful band slides off 100 MHz. EITHER restate FB2's requirement at its real operating current OR make FB2 a physically larger part. IR drop at 0.080 ohm max is 28.7 mV at the umbilical current (10.3 mW), 31.4 mV at the 392 mA module total, 3.6 mV at 45 mA. SECOND SOURCE: Murata BLM31PG601SN1L is an electrical twin and far better stocked, but its PDF carries no DC-bias curve either - that data lives only in SimSurfing - so it can be an alternate flagged 'bias assumed, not documented', never the characterised part. STOCK: the Laird part is out at LCSC (C2441375, 0). The named Murata twin BLM31PG601SN1L (LCSC C16902) is rated 1500 mA to 85 C and 1000 mA at 125 C [ds MURATA-BLM31-SN1-REFERENCE-SPEC-JENF243A-0006.pdf p.1] - fine at the module's currents - and publishes no DC-bias curve

description: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed
notes: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed. Its two companions are separate rows: the pass FET is Q-LOADSW and the sense resistor is R-ILIM. SUFFIX MATTERS: the -1 LATCHES OFF and is restored only by interrupting power or pulsing ON low; the -2 auto-retries at a 3.75% duty cycle into a persistent short. PINOUT: 1 ON, 2 FB, 3 PWRGD, 4 GND, 5 TIMER, 6 GATE, 7 SENSE, 8 VCC. *** FB, PIN 2, MUST BE DIVIDED DOWN FROM THE OUTPUT - NEVER LEFT OPEN. *** Foldback keys off V_FB, not off V_OUT ('the current folds back as a function of the output voltage, which is sensed at the FB pin', p.8), so with FB at 0V the limit sits at 12mV/50mohm = 240mA permanently, the output never charges, the timer ramps forever and the -1 latches. That is 'the instrument never starts', and no C-TIMER value fixes it; R-FB-HI/R-FB-LO are what set it. From the banked 164112fc.pdf: VCC UVLO 7.5 / 8.3 / 8.8 V, which holds GATE low regardless of ON; I_GATE -5 / -10 / -20 uA [p.2]; I_TIMER pull-up -24 / -80 / -132 uA [p.2]; the 12mV-to-47mV-at-VFB=0.5V law [Figure 7, p.9]. Package S8, theta-JA 110 degC/W. OPEN, AND DECIDED BY TEMPERATURE RATHER THAN BY THIS DOCUMENT: the grade. This row orders the CS8 (0 to +70degC); the IS8 is -40 to +85degC and is the better part for a rack that may sit in a hot van. That is a part change, not a documentation fix - decide it before the order

description: Sets the load switch current limit
notes: THE resistor that is the limit. 1.0A target. The stated 0.9-1.13A window is +-11% and is NARROWER THAN THE LT1641'S OWN SENSE-THRESHOLD TOLERANCE - the same mistake already found and fixed on the LM317 divider, one row down. So E6 measures the TRIP as well as the load, with a current probe, and the value is selected on the bench like R-REG-SET | 2026-09-21, from the banked 164112fc.pdf p.2: V_SENSETRIP is specified 39 / 47 / 55 mV (min/typ/max) at VFB=1V, i.e. +-17%. So R-ILIM at 50mohm gives a limit of 0.78 / 0.94 / 1.10 A. THE ROW'S OWN OBJECTION IS CONFIRMED BY THE DATASHEET: a +-11% window IS narrower than the part's own sense-threshold tolerance. The foldback floor at VFB=0 is 8/12/17mV, i.e. 160/240/340 mA - the low corner is what a hot-plug has to climb out of, and the worked start in power-entry.md uses the 12mV typ

description: Upper leg of the LT1641 FB divider, umbilical +12V to FB
notes: The FB divider. Its values and their derivation are the tracked figure loadswitch-fb-divider, owned by umbilical-load-switch.md and not restated here; what follows is what a reader of THIS row needs. FB must be divided down from the output at all - see U-LOADSW for why an open FB latches the part off. *** V_FB = 0.5V AND THE PWRGD THRESHOLD V_FBH = 1.313V ARE SET BY THE SAME DIVIDER, *** so V_OUT(full 47mV limit) = 0.381 x V_OUT(PWRGD) ALWAYS - 'cross 0.5V early in the ramp' and 'PWRGD means the output is good' are ONE decision, not two, and the ratio is fixed by the part, not by these resistors. It is therefore sized at the PWRGD end, which is the end with a hard requirement: PWRGD must release below the worst-case delivered output of ~11.36V (Eurorack +12V at -5%, less the sense and FET drops). The foldback law behind it, verbatim [p.5, drawn as Figure 7 p.9]: 'The current limit circuit will regulate the voltage across the sense resistor (VCC - VSENSE) to 47mV when VFB is 0.5V or higher. If VFB drops below 0.5V, the voltage across the sense resistor decreases linearly and stops at 12mV when VFB is 0V.' Divider current is 294uA at 12V, 294x the 1uA max FB input current [p.2], so leakage is <=0.34% of the ratio

description: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW
notes: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW. The value is the tracked figure loadswitch-timer and its derivation is in umbilical-load-switch.md; neither is restated here. TWO THINGS BIND WHEN BUYING IT. *** SPECIFY A LOW-LEAKAGE PART *** - at this value it is electrolytic or large ceramic, where leakage is a meaningful fraction of the 3 uA TIMER pull-down, and a leaky part means the timer never resets. And the package is through-hole radial or 1210 ceramic: an 0805 C0G cannot hold it. Fault time over the pull-up's own bounds is 587 / 160 / 95.6 ms, so the worst case is 95.6 ms against a 47.5 ms hot-plug start - 2.01x, which is the margin that actually had to be met. Datasheet hard minimum is 1.5 nF [p.5], not binding here

description: Gate capacitor programming the load switch ramp
notes: Programs the LT1641's output ramp: C = I_GATE / (dV/dt). The value and the ramp window it produces are the tracked figure loadswitch-gate-cap; do not restate them. THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE SIZING ANYTHING AROUND IT IS THAT I_GATE IS A 4:1 WINDOW - I_GATEUP = -5 / -10 / -20 uA [164112fc p.2], corroborated independently by the DC1354A demo quick-start guide p.1. *** SO ADR 0005's '50-100ms RAMP' IS NOT ACHIEVABLE WITH THIS PART: *** no single capacitor can hold a 4:1 current spread inside a 2:1 time window. The chosen value centres the TYPICAL inside ADR 0005 and the guaranteed envelope is wider. RAISED AGAINST ADR 0005 AND NOT DECIDED - either ADR 0005 widens the spec, or the ramp is programmed by something other than the internal pull-up. BOTH CORNERS ARE SAFE either way: 537mA of charging at the fast corner still clears the 240mA foldback floor at 0.14V of output and never approaches 940mA. C0G/NP0 or film, 50V - the dielectric matters, because a Y5V here re-programs the ramp with temperature. 1206 C0G, the same part as C-FILT-MOD: Murata GRM31C5C1H823JA01L, LCSC C97947 [ds MURATA-GRM31C5C1H823JA01L-82NF-C0G-1206.pdf]

notes: A PLAIN POWER LED off the module's own rail, like every other Eurorack module's. It used to be driven by a presence comparator that watched the breath line - that comparator is DELETED, and with it the only thing in the module that tried to know whether the instrument was there. Health reporting belongs in the instrument, which has a display, a web app and the actual data. With LT1641-1 latching off on a fault, this still says why the instrument went dark. PROPOSED: Lite-On LTL-4231N, LCSC C125082. ITS FLANGE IS D3.2, THE SAME AS THE PANEL HOLE [ds LITEON-LTL-4231N-3MM-GREEN-DIFFUSED.pdf p.2], so it does not stop against the panel: it needs MECH-LED-BEZEL-MOD

notes: ~4mA from the module's +12V analog rail. Was 820R from bus +5V when it shared a node with the level shifter's OE pins; that node is gone with the comparator

description: Hand-asserts the DAC8568 CLR during bring-up
notes: NORMALLY OPEN, AND IT IS COPPER - NOTHING IS ORDERED FOR THIS ROW, but the layout must carry the footprint. Two pads from CLR to AGND_MOD beside R-CLR-PU; shorting them pulls CLR low BY HAND, which is the only way to assert it - the watchdog that drove the net is not fitted and R-CLR-PU holds it inactive. E7-E10 pitch calibration wants a hand clear. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual assert parks every channel at zero scale

description: Pull-up holding the DAC8568 CLR inactive, with a bring-up pad
notes: THE WATCHDOG IS DELETED (U-WATCHDOG, R-WDT, C-WDT all gone), so CLR has no driver and is tied INACTIVE - pulled high. A solder pad to ground beside it lets CLR be asserted BY HAND, which E7-E10 want anyway: a 99ms watchdog would have fought every 'write a code, read the meter' step of pitch calibration. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual CLR still parks at zero scale. Do NOT write ClearIgnore

description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** LDAC MUST BE STRAPPED TO GND, NOT PULLED TO AVDD - PULLING IT HIGH GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38, verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' Same page: the internal LDAC register defaults to 0x00, and 'if the LDAC register bit is set to 0, the DAC channel is controlled by the LDAC pin'. So register at default plus pin high means the buffer-to-DAC-register transfer is BLOCKED - and with no MISO, firmware can never discover it. A module that accepts every word and moves no output. A hardware LDAC was considered and declined, so the six populated channels update as each word lands. WORTH REVISITING AT FIRMWARE TIME: SBAS430E Table 11 p.36 offers 'Write to DAC input register Ch X and update all DAC registers (SW LDAC)', so five plain writes then one update-all as the last word of each pass gives a SIMULTANEOUS update inside the six words already budgeted - taking the 100-200us CLR-exit window to zero for no parts and no ninth conductor

description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: *** THE ORDER CODE IS DAC8568ICPW(R), NOT DAC8568CIPW. *** Buy ICPWR, the reel of the same part: LCSC stocks it where it barely stocks ICPW [web 2026-09-29]. DAC8568CIPW appears ZERO times in SBAS430E; the Package Option Addendum [pp.54-57] enumerates DAC8568IAPW / IBPW / ICPW / IDPW and the R reel variants. The I and the grade letter are transposed in several places including the banked file's own NAME, datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf - the file and its SHA are correct and renaming it would mean editing another wave's manifest fragment, which CLAUDE.md 4 forbids, so the fact is recorded here per repo-maintenance.md 3. GRADE LOCKED TO C, and the letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state: A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything - pitch -2 to +2.25V, mods +/-5V - and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' *** THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V *** - C/D are specified only over that range where A/B are 2.7-5.5V. The LM317 nominal 5.21V passes, but E7 SELECTS R-REG-SET ON THE BENCH over a 0.66V worst-case spread, so 5.00V IS A HARD FLOOR ON THAT BENCH STEP. External VREFIN must be <= AVDD/2 on C/D against <= AVDD on A/B - not binding while the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit above ~2.6V. Reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT: C/D 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC against A/B 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs and Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, but BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle - enable at boot

description: Level shifter, 3V3 SPI up to 5V for the DAC
notes: SAME part as the instrument LED shifter. Covers SCLK MOSI CS with a spare gate. Runs from bus +5V; the DAC runs from U-REG-DAC. *** NO INPUT CLAMP TO VCC, *** confirmed three independent ways in SCLS264O: abs-max lists 'Input clamp current, IIK (VI < 0): -20mA', NEGATIVE ONLY, against an output clamp specified BOTH ways; abs-max input voltage is -0.5 to 7V stated WITHOUT reference to VCC where the output is -0.5 to VCC+0.5; and input leakage is specified as +/-1uA max AT VI = 5.5V WITH VCC = 0V, which TI could not guarantee if a VCC clamp existed. THAT IS WHAT MAKES BACK-DRIVING AN UNPOWERED MODULE SAFE. V_IH 2.0V min and V_IL 0.8V max are TTL levels, NOT ratioed to VCC - the threshold the R-SPI-SER analysis is built on. Drive +/-8mA; input transition rate must be <= 20ns/V; TIE EVERY UNUSED INPUT TO VCC OR GND. *** OE IS TIED ENABLED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. *** The presence-gated OE is deleted along with its comparator: the threshold sat inside the breath signal's own range, it locked out every standalone-module milestone, and it failed toward 'present'. What it was protecting against - floating CMOS at the DAC while the instrument is off - is what R-SPI-PULL's six resistors are for, and running the buffer unconditionally is what every surveyed Eurorack module does

description: Dual low-drift RRIO op-amp
notes: ONE op-amp part throughout the module, and THIS ROW IS WHERE THE OPA2197'S DEVICE FACTS LIVE - U-BUF and U-RESP cite it rather than repeat it. Six packages, twelve halves, TEN used: pitch, mod 1-4, mod offset follower, VREFOUT follower, breath REF-zero buffer, breath gain buffer, breath summer. TWO SPARE - and U-RESP claims both of them if it is fitted, so check that row before spending them. RRIO on +/-12V reaches ~11.9V. FROM THE BANKED SBOS737C: open-loop output impedance is SPECIFIED at 375 ohm [EC table p.8 and p.10, f = 1 MHz], with Figure 26 giving ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - *** DO NOT SIZE A POLE OFF THE 10MHz VALUE, *** which is roughly 5x optimistic. Capacitive load is 1 nF max [p.1 Features, 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'], and Figures 27/28 show that is a stable-but-RINGING limit, ~40% overshoot at unity gain - TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45/60 deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +/-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +/-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W - note the SINGLE OPA197 is 115.8 and is a different table. PSRR is +/-1 uV/V typ and +/-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case; the '114 dB' figure is not in the document

part: 10k multiturn cermet + divider from the LM317 5.21V rail
description: Nulls the sensor's +0.265V pedestal at the INA828 REF pin
notes: Buffered by a half of U-OPA-PITCH - REF needs a low source impedance or it degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** RANGE 0 TO +1.0V, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE PEDESTAL IS A SPEC BAND, NOT A TYPICAL *** - the datasheet's own table gives Voff 0.152 / 0.265 / 0.378 V, so the REF needed spans 0.332-0.826V. A 0.6V ceiling would leave a part at the top of its own spec UN-NULLABLE, with 1.4-5.6% of span standing at the jack; +1.0V covers the whole band with margin. The setting itself is the tracked figure breath-zero-ref; do not restate it. *** DERIVE IT FROM THE LM317'S 5.21V RAIL, NOT FROM VREFOUT. *** VREFOUT is the DAC's internal reference and is DISABLED at power-on until firmware writes an enable, so taking the breath zero from it would make the analog breath path depend on a DAC register - which three documents correctly say it does not. The LM317 rail is up whenever +12V is. THIS IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE PANEL KNOBS INDEPENDENT: with REF grounded the pedestal sits upstream of the gain pot and gets multiplied. One zero authority per representation still holds - this is CALIBRATION, set once, where the panel OFFSET knob is PERFORMANCE

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, and REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO THROUGH A BUFFER - never a bare divider, because source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** THE NUMBER IS 5 OHMS *** [SBOS792A section 8.1, verbatim: 'For the best performance, keep the source impedance to the REF terminal, RREF, below 5 ohm'] - RREF sits in series with one of the internal 40k difference-amp resistors and unbalances the bridge. Output runs 0V at rest to inamp-full-scale: Vout = -2.16106*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal. *** NOTE THE GAIN: 2.16106 IS THE EFFECTIVE GAIN, *** the raw G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185 times the 1M/(1M+11k) bias divider - using the raw 2.185 is the recorded way to get this wrong. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). EMI: the part HAS an integrated RFI filter, -3dB at 53MHz, and EMIRR is a TABULATED characteristic rather than just a curve. *** THE WORST CASES ARE 48dB DIFFERENTIAL AT 400MHz AND 51dB COMMON-MODE AT 1.8GHz, *** and the differential and common-mode columns INVERT between 900MHz (52/98) and 1.8GHz (94/51) - so any RF-rectification argument must use those two and not the 90-plus dB numbers. TI does not claim the internal filter is sufficient on its own. See breath-receive-stage.md

(4) Body 9.8mm wide, 11.4mm across the snap-in lugs, 7.0mm board-to-shaft for every -40, shaft D6.0 0/-0.1 - three across 50.50mm is 34.2mm, so the pot body is nowhere near binding and the 14mm knob is the constraint. description: Nonlinear element for the response shaper
notes: Breath is unipolar so only one ever conducts in play; the second covers the power-on and fault excursions. Scaling is set at /2 so the knee lands at about a quarter of a hard blow - at /10 it would sit ABOVE the playing range and the control would do nothing until you overblow. *** THE 0.6 V KNEE THIS SHAPER DEPENDS ON IS NOT-IN-DOCUMENT AS A SPEC. *** Neither banked datasheet specifies V_F at 0.6V; it is readable only off Vishay's TYPICAL Fig.1 (~1mA at 25degC), and that curve shifts more than 100mV LEFT at 150degC - on a part whose entire behaviour is where the knee sits. The tightest SPECIFIED bound in the bank is Diotec's V_F < 0.855V at 10mA, still 250mV above the asserted knee. *** NAME THE MANUFACTURER WHEN ORDERING: *** Vishay's 1N4148W (Document 86356 Rev 1.0) is a true SOD-123 - 2.7 x 1.55mm body, 3.7mm overall, 1.175mm high, R-thJA 440 K/W, P_tot 280mW on the recommended footprint, I_F(AV) 250mA, V_F <=1V at 10mA, C_D 1.5pF max, t_rr 4ns - while Diotec's same-numbered part is SOD-123F, flat lead, no standoff. Use Vishay's 440 K/W / 280mW as the conservative thermal pair; Diotec's 312 K/W / 400mW assume 3mm2 of copper per terminal. The plain 1N4148 is NEITHER package: it is leaded glass SOD27 (DO-35) axial. Which of the two SMD sizes to use is open and is decided by the board - either is electrically identical here

description: Pitch gain trimmer, in series with R2 of the LT5400 pair
notes: 200R, not 1k. In series with R2 it is 0 to +2% of the ratio, and its ~100ppm/degC then contributes ~2ppm/degC - COMPARABLE to the LT5400 rather than 4-20x it, which was ADR 0006's own objection to its own trimmer. Two percent is enough now that pitch feedback is tapped at the jack and the load divider is gone; firmware's per-load affine covers the remainder

description: Pitch offset trimmer, AHEAD of the VREFOUT follower
notes: MOVED. It now trims the reference the follower buffers, so it scales the intercept (k x V_ref) and touches the gain (1 + k) NOT AT ALL - a genuinely independent offset trim. R-OFFINJ is deleted with it: injecting into the inverting node was never a pure offset, because in a non-inverting stage that node sits at Vdac rather than at a virtual ground, so it added ~1% of gain and its span was one-sided. Range ~50mV on a 2.5V reference is ~60 cents of offset

description: Compensation cap, op-amp OUTPUT to the inverting input
notes: FROM THE OP-AMP OUTPUT TO THE (-) INPUT. NOT 'across the feedback resistor' - with the tap at the jack, R2 spans jack-to-(-), so a cap across R2 connects the same two nodes and leaves R-OUT-PROT inside the loop at every frequency: 18 degrees of phase margin with 2m of cable, under 10 with four destinations. Three documents said 'across R2' and were wrong. 2.2nF with C-FILT-PITCH restored is maximally flat, -3dB at 12.2kHz. IT IS NOT A FILTER: a cap in the feedback of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC), a pole and a zero an octave up, flattening at unity - 6.02dB maximum for any value. Two independent reviews found this separately

description: Anti-alias/glitch filter on the pitch DAC input, ahead of the op-amp
notes: THE ACTUAL PITCH FILTER. 15.9kHz against R-OPAMP-IN's 1k, on a node with NO LOOP AROUND IT. C-FB-PITCH cannot do this job: a cap across the feedback resistor of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC) - a pole at 15.9kHz and a zero an octave above, flattening at unity, so 6.02dB of attenuation maximum for any value. It is a shelf, not a pole. Filtering the DAC before the stage is also what the surveyed designs do

part: Range-setting resistors for the two module trimmers
description: Sets TRIM-OFFSET's and TRIM-BREATH-ZERO's spans
notes: Both trimmers need a divider to set their span and neither had parts. TRIM-OFFSET wants ~+-50mV around 2.500V; TRIM-BREATH-ZERO wants 0 to +1.0V from the LM317 rail. Values with the stages at E10

description: Reconstruction and RF shunt at the pitch jack
notes: RESTORED. It was deleted on the reasoning that a cap on the feedback node sits inside the DC loop at the handover; two independent loop analyses then put 10nF there and found phase margin UNCHANGED, because C-FB-PITCH ties the (-) input to the op-amp OUTPUT so beta(inf)=1 and R-OUT-PROT isolates the jack above the handover. The feedback network is a LEAD at every load tried - open, 200pF, 800pF, 10nF, dead short. Deleting it cost 30dB at 1MHz and left the connector with no low-impedance shunt at all

description: DC bias path to ground at every DAC output pin
notes: AT THE DAC PIN, not after R-OPAMP-IN - 100k after the 1k would form a divider and cost 1% of gain. Without it the op-amp (+) inputs have no DC path to ground: their only connection is a DAC pin that may be high-Z before power-on reset, so outputs can sit at either rail during that window. The identical problem was already found and fixed on the breath in-amp (R-BIAS-INAMP); this is the same fix on the six DAC-driven nodes

description: Matched resistor network for pitch scaling
package: MSOP-8 MS8E (0.65mm pitch) WITH 1.88 x 1.68mm EXPOSED PAD
notes: RATIO IS 1:1 - the pitch stage is a non-inverting amp with the reference at the bottom of the feedback divider (see pitch-stage.md). Two of four sections used. ORDER CODE IS TWO LETTER FIELDS: LT5400 + <A|B matching> + <C|I|H|MP temp> + MS8E-1#PBF. The -1 option is the four-equal-10k 1:1 quad and THERE IS NO 1:3 OPTION [p.2 table: -1 10k 1:1, -2 100k 1:1, -3 1:10, -4 1k 1:1, -5 1M 1:1, -6 1:5]. Grade A is 0.01% matching, B 0.025%; A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat. MUST BE THE MS8 (MSOP) OPTION, NOT THE LEADLESS DFN. *** MS8E HAS AN EXPOSED PAD *** [p.2, p.8] - the footprint is MSOP-8-1EP_3x3mm_P0.65mm_EP1.68x1.88mm, NOT a plain MSOP-8. WHERE THE PAD GOES [p.6]: not DC-connected to any resistor, 'do not tie the exposed pad to noisy signals or noisy grounds', 'connecting the exposed pad to a quiet AC ground is recommended'. OPEN, AND IT IS A LAYOUT DECISION NOBODY HAS MADE: pad-to-resistor coupling is 5.5 pF against 1.4 pF resistor-to-resistor, so THE PAD IS THE DOMINANT STRAY ON THE 1V/OCT NODE and nothing in this corpus says where it connects. Ratio tracking 1 ppm/degC MAX (0.2 typ). ABSOLUTE tolerance is +/-7.5% (A) / +/-15% (B), which sets TRIM-GAIN's real authority at 1.86-2.16% rather than a nominal 2%. WHY THE PART IS KEPT, since its own tempco is currently masked: the DAC's internal reference drifts 0.42 cents over 10degC and cannot be trimmed, against 0.027 for the LT5400 and 0.38 for two 0.1%/10ppm discretes - $8 permanently solves the one term that can be, on a board built once, and attacking the reference later is only worth doing if the network is already there. CAVEAT FOR ANYONE EDITING ADR 0006: the banked rev fa's option table ends at -6, so LT5400-7 and 'a 1:4 offered directly' are NOT-IN-DOCUMENT rather than refuted - do not 'correct' ADR 0006 by citing rev fa's silence. 5400fc.pdf is still wanted. *** STATUS MOVED selected -> open 2026-09-22: THE ORDER CODE IS INCOMPLETE. *** LT5400<A|B><C|I|H|MP>MS8E-1#PBF needs BOTH letters and neither is chosen anywhere in this corpus. DECIDED BY TWO THINGS, both cheap: matching grade A 0.01% against B 0.025% - and note A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat, so A is not simply better - and the temperature grade, where C is 0 to +70degC in a rack that may sit in a hot van, the same argument already made for U-LOADSW's grade. A row marked 'selected' that cannot be put in a basket is the defect this status exists to prevent

description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.. 82nF C0G 50V EXISTS IN 1206: Murata GRM31C5C1H823JA01L, LCSC C97947 [ds MURATA-GRM31C5C1H823JA01L-82NF-C0G-1206.pdf]

description: Feedback leg (R2) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R2 of each channel. R2/R1 = k = 3, so gain = 1+k = EXACTLY 4 and the intercept is k x V_ref with V_ref = 3.3333V from the offset channel - which lands the window on exactly +-10.000V. EIGHT RESISTORS FOR FOUR CHANNELS, not sixteen: do not order a four-resistor difference-amp set. Tolerance is worst case +-50.5mV of zero and -1.49/+1.52 percent of span, and same-sign parts cancel in the ratio, which is the reason for one series and TCR grade (R-MODGAIN-IN)

description: Input leg (R1) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R1 of each channel, and it goes to the SHARED buffered reference from DAC ch7, NOT to ground - that is what makes a CLR park every jack at 0V. Four, one per channel. It is the RATIO with R-MODGAIN-FB that has to hold, not either absolute value: buy both from ONE SERIES AND TCR GRADE, Yageo RT0805BRD07 (0.1%, 25 ppm/C), which holds the ratio to 0.2% [calc] - two values cannot come off one reel

notes: Laser or waterjet from mechanical/module/export/panel.dxf (generated from config/module.yaml; ADR 0024) - SAME vendor and order as the key plate. 10HP (ADR 0004). THE HEIGHT BUDGET IS THE TRACKED FIGURE panel-height-budget - do not restate it here. The toggle's shaped hole is panel-toggle-hole; there is no PUSH-tab slot

description: Series protection on each CV output
notes: *** SPECIFY 0.66-1W IN 1206 (ERJ-P08 class, confirmed to exist). THE POWER RATING IS NOT OPTIONAL AND THIS IS THE ONLY PART IN THE MODULE AT REAL RISK FROM ANY JACK FAULT. *** The worst case is output-to-output patching, not a short: with pitch taking jack-side feedback the loop FIGHTS the other module, giving 322mW against a 220R source at +/-10V (two reviewers found this independently, on 269/312/464mW ladders). A dead short merely rails the op-amp across this resistor, at 142mW. AND THE DERATING IS WHAT RULES OUT 500mW: thick-film at a 50C rack interior leaves a 500mW 1206 delivering 350-420mW, so it is ~1.1x margin, not the 2.6x a nameplate reading suggests. Mutable specifies its output 1k at >=200mW where every other resistor in the same BOM is 100mW, which is the published form of this argument

description: Series resistor on each op-amp + input driven by the DAC
notes: SEVEN. Now correct on the mod channels as well, because the two-resistor form drives the op-amp's (+) input directly - a true high-Z node where 1k causes no error. It was wrong on the OLD four-resistor version, where the 10k input resistor WAS the gain network and 1k in series unbalanced it. Pitch, mod 1-4, the mod offset buffer, the VREFOUT follower. DAC on 5.21V and op-amps on +-12V do not come up together; bounds clamp current, outside the feedback path so no accuracy cost

description: Clamp diodes on the DRIVER side of R-OUT-PROT
notes: MOVED to the op-amp side of the 1k, which fixes two things at once. (a) BACK-POWERING: clamped at the JACK, a neighbouring module driving 10V through its own 220R output pushes 42mA per jack into our +12V rail when this module is off - 254mA across six jacks, into the rail that also feeds the umbilical. Behind the 1k it is 7.6mA per jack. (b) LEAKAGE: inside the feedback loop the op-amp absorbs it, so the 2.4-cent BAT54S error goes to identically zero for any diode. BAV99 kept anyway - silicon costs nothing and the reasoning no longer depends on it. NOTE: no surveyed design clamps a CV output to the RAILS at all; every clamp in the corpus goes to GND. Erica Synths is the one that puts its clamp on the driver side, which is where this now is. SIX - one per OUTPUT jack including breath, whose schematic omitted it. The two BREATH INPUT clamps are a separate row, D-CLAMP-BREATH, so the module carries eight BAV99 in total

description: 3.5mm mono PCB-mount jack
notes: De facto eurorack standard. BUSHING IS D6.0mm WITH 4.5mm OF THREAD, so the panel hole is 6mm nominal and 6.2-6.5 in practice, with 5.5mm from the panel face to the body front including the shoulder. Body 9 x 9 x 8.3mm, barrel bore D3.6, 3.5mm of tails behind. Rated DC30V 0.5A, 5000 cycles, PBT / brass-Ni / BeCu-Ag. *** PINOUT, cross-checked two ways (drawing schematic, and a KiCad footprint whose pads are NAMED with offsets matching the drawing's 4.92 / 3.38 / 6.48): PIN 3 = TIP, PIN 2 = TIP-NORMAL SWITCH CONTACT - NORMALLY CLOSED TO PIN 3 AND OPENING WHEN A PLUG IS INSERTED - PIN 1 = SLEEVE. *** All three on one centreline, oval drill 1.6 x 0.6. LEAVE A 3mm HOLE OR A VOID IN THE PCB UNDER THE BARREL (Thonk's own note). THE SWITCH CONTACT IS FREE NORMALLING and nothing in the design uses it yet - worth knowing before the layout rather than after. FILED AT BOARD LEVEL, beside R-OUT-PROT, because three circuits drive these six jacks and panel.md owns only the cutouts: no single circuit page derives the connector

description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: *** GAUGE IS OPEN AND THREE DERIVATIONS ASSUME 24 AWG. *** 0005:91 computes a ~0.34 ohm round trip, breath-sense-link.md:100 a 0.168 ohm return term, and 0003:315 a whole signal-drop table - all at 24 AWG, which this row does not specify. description: Tail-end cap carrying the etherCON and the USB-C slot
notes: OAK, so the wood reads as wrapping from the top face around the bottom and up the back. The etherCON exits this face AXIALLY - straight out along the long axis, the way a flute foot joint is open at the end (ADR 0004) - so a 2m tether hangs rather than twists. The connector allows a 3mm panel at most, so a recess routed into the outside face leaves that much oak where it mounts: the PUSH tab stands in the recess - mechanical/drc.echo 'tail cap recess for the etherCON inside the tail face'. It stands on the floor, so the oak above and below the bore is in mechanical/drc.echo. Beside the flange: the USB-C receptacle's slot, on end, at the bottom of an overmould-sized pocket routed into the tail face (config/body.yaml openings.usb_overmold, usb_panel_t) - the DXF carries the slot and the bore; the pocket and the recess are router passes

description: Oak-to-oak lamination: spacer layers and the thumb rest lip
notes: The only wood-to-wood joints in the stack, and the strongest and cheapest joint available. Does NOT bond aluminium or acrylic, which is half the reason the old single MECH-ADHESIVE row could not have worked

part: RTV silicone - ALKOXY (alcohol) neutral cure, electronics-safe
description: Plate to oak, matrix diffuser, thumb plate - and the lid gasket
notes: NOT ACETOXY. The common hardware-store type releases acetic acid while curing, inside a sealed cavity holding two dev boards, a carrier, connectors and a pressure sensor. Compliant in shear so the oak's 0.6-0.9mm of cross-grain humidity movement does not fight the aluminium plate; stiff in compression so the plate is still backed under a key press. BEAD IT, DO NOT BUTTER IT - cure needs atmospheric moisture and runs ~2mm/day inwards, so a trapped full-face layer never cures. Keep it off both sensor ports (ADR 0003), and bond the plate only after both key boards are mounted on its studs and soldered (ADR 0020, Amendment 4); the beads may run over the studs' flush heads | 2026-09-21: TWO JOBS NOW. Adhesive on the permanent joints above; GASKET on the lid-to-U joint, which opens on six fasteners (ADR 0009). Same tube. Lay the gasket bead on ONE face, let it skin, then clamp - a fresh bead glues the lid shut, which is the failure this change exists to avoid

description: Spare dev board, bought with the original
notes: BUY IT WITH THE ORIGINAL, not later. ADR 0013 names a discontinued dev board as a redesign risk and the vendor ships silent revisions. A spare DOES rescue a bricked instrument now that the body opens on six fasteners (ADR 0009) - this row said it could not, which was true while the body was bonded. Still insurance against a dead board during BUILD and bring-up, and against the part vanishing before M8

Shortest that reaches from the Matrix board to the tail cap with slack for the cap to come off - mechanical/drc.echo gives the run. Receptacle mounts ON END in the tail cap (openings.usb_slot_portrait) and must be EARLESS, clamped against the cap from behind (openings.usb_mount): on end, screw ears land outside the cavity (mechanical/drc.echo, USB-C receptacle mount inside the cavity).
